name: Opsgenie
description: The Opsgenie App provides at-a-glance views and detailed analytics for alerts on your DevOps environment, allowing you to effectively monitor and gain valuable insights into your incidents and incident handling operations. Opsgenie is an incident management platform for operating services that are on 24/7. Opsgenie allows you to plan for service disruptions and stay in control during incidents. Opsgenie centralizes alerts and reliably notifies the correct contacts to ensure timely analysis and efficient action.

queries.queryString:
_sourceCategory = Labs/Opsgenie_alerts Create
| json "alert.createdAt", "alert.description", "alert.message", "action", "alert.team",  "alert.priority", "alert.source" , "alert.tags[*]","alert.recipients[*]" as created_at, description, message, action, team, priority, source, tags, recipients nodrop
| where action = "Create" and priority matches "{{priority}}"
| timeslice 1h
| count by _timeslice, priority
| transpose row _timeslice column priority

panels.title: Top 10 Alerts with the Slowest Time to Close

queries.queryString:
_sourceCategory = Labs/Opsgenie_alerts Close
| json "alert.createdAt", "alert.updatedAt" , "alert.description", "alert.message", "action", "alert.username",  "alert.priority", "alert.source" , "alert.tags[*]","alert.recipients[*]", "alert.details" as created_at, updated_at, description, message, action, username, priority, source, tags, recipients, alert_details nodrop
| where action = "Close"and priority matches "{{priority}}"
| updated_at/1000000 as epoch_updated_at
| (epoch_updated_at - created_at)/(1000*3600) as hours_to_close_alert 
//| round(hours_to_close_alert,5) as hours_to_close_alert
| count by  message, priority, source, username, hours_to_close_alert
| sort by hours_to_close_alert 
| fields - _count 
| limit 10

queries.queryString:
_sourceCategory = Labs/Opsgenie_alerts Create
| json "alert.createdAt", "alert.description", "alert.message", "action", "alert.team",  "alert.priority", "alert.source" , "alert.tags[*]","alert.recipients[*]" as created_at, description, message, action, team, priority, source, tags, recipients nodrop
| where action = "Create"
| formatDate(fromMillis(created_at), "MM-dd-yyyy HH:mm:ss") as Created_date_time
| count by Created_date_time, description, message, action, team, priority, source, tags, recipients
| sort by _count
| fields - _count

| timeslice 1h
| count by _timeslice
| outlier _count window=10,threshold=3,consecutive=2,direction=+
